summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of kidney transplantation was admitted after recording a low blood pressure of 80/50 at home on the first postoperative day following a lumpectomy. She had been NPO the night before surgery and had minimal oral intake afterward. She presented with weakness and lightheadedness but was stable in the emergency department. Her hypotension was attributed to volume depletion from poor oral intake and continuation of antihypertensive medications, including a diuretic. She was managed with IV fluids, and her home antihypertensives—Lasix and Valsartan—were held. Blood pressure normalized during the hospital stay. Blood and urine cultures were obtained due to immunosuppression but showed no signs of infection. An ophthalmology consult was arranged at the patient’s request due to recent vitreous hemorrhage; the exam was normal with no active bleeding or elevated intraocular pressure. She was discharged home with adjusted antihypertensive therapy, continuing all other baseline medications, including immunosuppressants and insulin. Follow-up was arranged with her transplant team to reassess blood pressure management.
